# Closed-shell command reference

Every command of the closed shell (`sneakers-shell`), the login shell of every admin over SSH and
the menu on the console, as `help` shows it. How the shell splits a line, its errors and the
root shell are in [ssh-and-elevation.md](ssh-and-elevation.md#the-closed-shell). `<product>`
stands for the installed product's name (`sneakers`), and `<value>` for each value it exposes
to the login's role.

The appliance's closed shell: the commands below, nothing else. help <command> shows a command's purpose, what it takes and an example; -o json prints a result, or an error, as JSON.

Every command takes `-o json` (`--output json`).

## `<product>`

<Product> commands.

The commands of <Product>, the installed product. They're offered only while it's installed.

Offered over: SSH and console.

```text
<product> <command>
```

Its commands:

- `<product> <value>`: <Value label> (shown to the roles the product names)
- `<product> mcp`: Show or set the MCP switch, the one the MCP card on :8443 sets

Example:

```text
  <product> <value>
  <product> mcp
```

## `<product> <value>`

<Value label> (shown to the roles the product names).

Shows <Value label>, a value the installed product exposes to your role, with the link that takes it. A one-time value is removed once it has been used; after that this says so. Over SSH only.

Offered over: SSH.

```text
<product> <value>
```

Example:

```text
  <product> <value>
```

## `<product> mcp`

Show or set the MCP switch, the one the MCP card on :8443 sets.

Without arguments it shows the installed product's MCP switch and its machine API switch. on or off sets the MCP switch; the machine API keeps its setting unless the line names it with machine-api=on or machine-api=off. The switches are the ones the product declares, the same ones the MCP card on :8443 sets, under the same role and audit.

Offered over: SSH and console.

```text
<product> mcp [on|off] [machine-api=on|off]
```

Example:

```text
  <product> mcp
  <product> mcp on
  <product> mcp off machine-api=off
```

Help about any command.

## `keys`

Login keys.

The admins' SSH login keys. Keys are issued on :8443.

Offered over: SSH and console.

```text

```

Its commands:

- `keys list`: List login keys

Example:

```text

```

## `keys list`

List login keys.

Lists an admin's SSH login keys: fingerprint, type and comment. Without --admin it lists your own; an owner may name any admin. Keys are issued on :8443.

Offered over: SSH and console.

```text
keys list [flags]
```

| Flag | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--admin` | the admin (owners only; default yourself) |

Example:

```text
  keys list
  keys list --admin alice
```

## `network`

Network settings.

The network settings: show them, change them (with an automatic revert) and keep a change.

Offered over: SSH and console.

```text
network <command>
```

Its commands:

- `network allow-list`: The management allow-list
- `network confirm`: Keep a pending network change
- `network set`: Change network settings (reverts in 120 s unless confirmed)
- `network show`: Show the network settings

Example:

```text
  network allow-list reset
  network confirm 7K2Q-MX4D
  network set ?
  network show
```

## `network allow-list`

The management allow-list.

The management allow-list, the networks that may reach SSH and :8443.

Offered over: SSH and console.

```text
network allow-list <command>
```

Its commands:

- `network allow-list reset`: Reset the management allow-list to the on-link default

Example:

```text
  network allow-list reset
```

## `network allow-list reset`

Reset the management allow-list to the on-link default.

Sets the management allow-list back to the subnets the box is on, for when a wrong list locks SSH and :8443 out. Console only; type reset to confirm. It reverts in 120 seconds unless kept with network confirm.

Offered over: console.

```text
network allow-list reset
```

Example:

```text
  network allow-list reset
```

## `network confirm`

Keep a pending network change.

Keeps the network change the token names, so it doesn't revert. network set and network allow-list reset print the token.

Offered over: SSH and console.

```text
network confirm <token>
```

Example:

```text
  network confirm 7K2Q-MX4D
```

## `network set`

Change network settings (reverts in 120 s unless confirmed).

Changes the settings the keys name, on top of the current ones; the others stay as they are. The change is applied at once and reverts after 120 seconds unless it's kept: the command asks, or run network confirm with the token it prints. Owners only. With no arguments, or ?, it lists the keys. The interfaces' addresses are set on :8443 or the console's network screen.

Offered over: SSH and console.

```text
network set key=value...
```

| Key | Meaning | Example |
|---|---|---|
| `hostname=` | the box's host name | `hostname=box1.sneakers.example.org` |
| `dns=` | the DNS servers, comma-separated; empty clears them | `dns=192.0.2.53,192.0.2.54` |
| `search=` | the DNS search domains, comma-separated | `search=sneakers.example.org` |
| `ntp=` | the NTP servers, comma-separated | `ntp=192.0.2.123,time.example.org` |
| `allow-list=` | the networks that may reach SSH and :8443, comma-separated CIDRs | `allow-list=192.0.2.0/24,198.51.100.0/24` |
| `time-zone=` | the time zone the box shows times in, an IANA name | `time-zone=America/New_York` |
| `https-proxy=` | the proxy for outbound HTTPS, a URL; empty for none | `https-proxy=http://192.0.2.8:3128` |

Example:

```text
  network set ?
  network set dns=192.0.2.53,192.0.2.54 search=sneakers.example.org
  network set time-zone=America/New_York
  network set https-proxy=
```

## `network show`

Show the network settings.

Shows the host name, the management addresses, DNS servers and search domains, NTP servers, the management allow-list, the time zone and the HTTPS proxy.

Offered over: SSH and console.

```text
network show
```

Example:

```text
  network show
  network show -o json
```

## `recovery-key`

Recovery keys.

The recovery keys, which open the box when no admin can.

Offered over: SSH and console.

```text

```

Its commands:

- `recovery-key add`: Add a recovery key, read from standard input (up to three)

Example:


## `recovery-key add`

Add a recovery key, read from standard input (up to three).

Adds a recovery key, an SSH public key read from standard input, and writes a new escrow file. Console only; a box keeps up to three.

Offered over: console.

```text
recovery-key add [flags]
```

| Flag | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--label` | a label such as "offline safe" |

Example:

```text
  recovery-key add --label "offline safe"
```

First boot setup.

The steps of first boot that are done over SSH.

## `setup recovery-key`

Set a recovery key during setup, read from standard input.

Sets the first recovery key during setup: an SSH public key read from standard input. Over SSH, first boot only; it writes a new escrow file.

Offered over: SSH.

```text

```

| Flag | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--label` | a label such as "offline safe" |

Example:

```text

```

## `shell`

Open the root shell (root operators): a challenge, then the code :8443 gives for it.

Opens the root shell, for root operators. It prints a challenge; paste it on the Root shell page on :8443, give a fresh authenticator code there, and type the code that page gives you here. The session is time-boxed, recorded and audited. Needs a terminal (ssh -t).

Offered over: SSH.

```text
shell [flags]
```

| Flag | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--reason` | why, for the audit log |

Example:

```text
  shell --reason "check the k0s pods"
```

## `status`

Show the appliance status.

Shows the host name, the version (and any staged one), the phase, the disk protection, the management addresses, NTP and the health of each service, with any warnings. While the appliance services are down it shows the last status they kept, with its time.

Offered over: SSH and console.

```text
status
```

Example:

```text
  status
  status -o json
```

## `updates`

Show or set the channel the GitHub update source follows, as the mirror card on :8443 does.

Shows the update source, the channel the GitHub source follows (stable, or rc, which takes a newer stable too), the repository and the release last picked. updates channel sets the channel, and default goes back to this build's own (rc on a pre-release build). updates repo points a lab build at a test repository; a production build refuses it. Owners only for a change.

Offered over: SSH and console.

```text
updates [channel rc|stable|default] [repo <owner>/<name>|default]
```

Example:

```text
  updates
  updates channel rc
  updates channel default
  updates repo example/test-releases
```

## `upgrade`

Upgrades.

Stages and applies updates from the shell. Not available in this release; updates are done on :8443.

Offered over: SSH and console.

```text

```

Example:

